declared.title: What is more important for national well-being: Money or autonomy? A meta-analysis of well-being, burnout, and anxiety across 63 societies
declared.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
declared.foundIn: rapport contre-preuve reports/too-many-choices/counter-evidence.md (2026-11-22), DOI trouvé par ses requêtes ; titre relevé sur Crossref par la session : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: national samples from 63 countries (420,599 people), measures of ill-being, anxiety and stress; countries not listed in the abstract

findings.text: Across 63 countries, more individualistic (autonomy-granting) societies had more well-being, more consistently than richer ones

support.sentence: Despite some emerging nonlinear trends and interactions between wealth and individualism, the overall pattern strongly suggests that greater individualism is consistently associated with more well-being.

limits: an association between countries, not people's own choices
individualism and autonomy, not the number of options
whether Arab countries are among the 63 is not given in the abstract
